texts.facts: Vide this judgmentcumaward, I proceed to decide the DAR which is treated as petition u/s 166 and 140 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, as amended uptodate (hereinafter referred to as the Act) for grant of compensation in a road accident. 2. It is the case of the petitioner that on 25.06.2014 at about 08:00 p.m., the petitioner was going to the market to purchase vegetable on foot. As soon as she reached near Kailashpuri Chowk, all of a sudden a water tanker bearing No.DL1LS7154 came from Sagarpur side and was going towards Indra Park in a very high speed and was driven in a very rash and negligent manner and it hit the petitioner/injured very badly. Due to the powerful impact, the injured fell down on the road and Bimla Devi vs Jujjar Singh on 4 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47206546/ 1 sustained multiple grievous injuries on various parts of her body. It is contended that the accident was caused due to the sole negligence on the part of the respondent No.1 who is the driver of the offending vehicle and caused injuries to the petitioner, however the driver of the offending vehicle tried to flee away from the spot of accident but was caught hold of by the public persons. It is stated that in respect of the accident, FIR No.275/14, under sections 279/338/465/471 IPC was lodged at PS Sagarpur against the driver of the offending vehicle. Suit No. D464/14 3. It is submitted that the petitioner got fracture in the first and second finger/right MT and great toe of her right foot and the right foot of the petitioner was injured badly and about 20 stitches were put by the doctors on her foot. After the accident, the petitioner was taken to Ansari Hospital, Sagarpur, Delhi where she remained admitted from 25.06.2014 to 26.06.2014 and the MLC of the petitioner was prepared by the doctors vide MLC No.082/14. Due to the fracture in her right foot, a plaster was put. It is averred that at the time of the accident, the petitioner was 61 years old and was performing her household work/ obligations very well but due to the injuries sustained by her, she was not able to do her daily routine work and she had to hire an attendant for herself and was giving Rs.5,000/ per month for a period of about five months. It is averred that on the advice of the doctors for her early recovery, the petitioner had to take special diet for which she had to spend a sum of Rs. 300/ per day. The petitioner had already spent a sum of Rs.25,000/ (approximately) upon conveyance. It is submitted that due to the injuries, the injured as well as her family members had to suffer great mental pain, agony and financial hardship. Due to the accident, the injured had become permanently disabled as her fingers of the right foot were not working/ moving. 4. Reply to DAR was filed on behalf of the respondent No.1 stating therein that on 25.06.2014 at about 08:00 pm, the water tanker No.DL1LS7154 owned by M/s City Life Line Travels Pvt. Ltd. and driven by the respondent No. 1 was going towards Sadh Nagar, Delhi. It is submitted that the tanker was Suit No. D464/14 driven by the respondent No.1 after following all the traffic rules and regulations as applicable at that time. It is stated that the tanker had valid route permit and fitness certificate till 16.06.2018 and the respondent No.1 had a valid driving license to drive the tanker on 2 5 . 0 6 . 2 0 1 4 . 3 v i d e p o l i c y No.350300/31/14/6300001265 valid from 07.06.2014 to 06.06.2015 . It is averred that as per the information provided by the respondent No.1 the accident took place at 08:00 p.m on 25.06.2014. It is contended that the vehicle No.DL1LS7154 was on the correct side of the road and was moving at moderate speed and the accident took place due to the negligence of the petitioner who came in front of the bus all of a sudden on the road. It is submitted that there was no willful violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy which was supplied by the insurance company at the time of taking the policy. Reply to DAR was filed on behalf of the respondent No.2 taking the same pleas as taken in the reply filed on behalf of the respondent No.1. It was further averred that the respondent No.2 had appointed the respondent No.1 as driver after going through the driving license produced by him which appeared to be genuine one. The respondent No.2 had also taken the test of driving skill of the respondent No.1 and was satisfied with his driving. 5. Written statement was filed on behalf of the respondent No.3 taking the preliminary objections that the respondent No.1 was driving the vehicle No.DL1LS7154 (TATA407) at the time of the accident and he was not holding Suit No. D464/14 a valid and effective driving license for driving Bimla Devi vs Jujjar Singh on 4 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47206546/ 2 the vehicle on the road at the time of the alleged accident. It is contended that the petitioner has not come with clean hands before the court and has approached the court with malafide intentions to extract money from the respondent No.3. It is denied that the vehicle No.DL1LS7154 was being driven by the driver very rashly and negligently, thereby hitting the injured and causing the alleged injuries. It is averred that the driver of the offending vehicle was driving his vehicle on the correct side and that too in normal speed, but it was the mistake of the injured who suddenly crossed the road without seeing the traffic on the road. The injured grossly and intentionally violated the traffic rules and regulations due to which the alleged accident might have happened. It is stated that no cause of action lay in favour of the petitioner and against the respondent No.3, since the accident as alleged did not occur because of the negligence of the respondent No.1, however, the accident occurred because of the negligence of the injured/ petitioner herself. It is submitted that the contract of insurance is based on the principle of indemnity and if the insured wants to take benefit under the policy, then he shall prove that the vehicle was not being used in contravention of the insurance policy (valid DL, RC, willful negligence, immediate notice of accident to the insurer etc.) and in case he failed to prove so then no liability could be fastened upon the respondent No.3. It is admitted that the policy No. 350300/31/14/6300001265 valid for period from 00.00 hours on 07.06.2014 to midnight 06.06.2015 for the vehicle No.DL1LS7154 was issued in the name of City Life Line Travels Pvt. Ltd. on certain terms and conditions of the policy. It Suit No. D464/14 is averred that the claim of the petitioner is baseless, incorrect and does not have any material against the insurance company. 6. From the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed vide order dated 20.01.2015: 1. OPP 2. If so, to what amount and from whom? 3. Relief. The matter was adjourned sine die vide order dated 25.3.2015. The matter was restored vide order dated 1.7.2015. An application for issuance of disability certificate was filed on behalf of the petitioner which was allowed vide order dated 1.7.2015. Thereafter, report was received from the Disability Board as per which the petitioner was a case of united fracture 1st, 2nd metatarsal right foot and the patient had no permanent disability. 7. The petitioner Smt. Bimla Devi herself appeared in the witness box as PW1 and led her evidence by way of affidavit which is Ex.PW1/1. Copy Suit No. D464/14 of the treatment documents, medical bills, discharge slip and MLC are Ex.PW1/A (colly), DAR is Ex.PW1/B and election card is Ex.PW1/C. PE was closed on 26.9.2015. texts.arguments: As the case is U/s 166 M.V Act it was incumbent upon the petitioner to prove that she sustained injuries in an accident caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle. To determine the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle it has been held in National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Pushpa Rana & Another 2009 Accident Claims Journal 287 as follows: "The last contention of the appellant insurance company is that the respondents/claimants should have proved negligence on the part of the driver and in this regard the counsel has placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. V. Meena Variyal (supra). On perusal of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced: (i) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in FIR No.955 of 2004, pertaining to involvement of offending vehicle (ii) criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of charge sheet under sections 279/304A, Indian Penal Code against the driver; (iii) certified copy of FIR, wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical Suit No. D464/14 inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of deceased. These documents are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent. Proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard. Hence, this contention of the counsel Bimla Devi vs Jujjar Singh on 4 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47206546/ 4 for the appellant also falls face down. There is ample evidence on record to prove negligence on part of the driver." In Kaushnamma Begum and others v. New India Assurance Company Limited, it was inter alia held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that the issue of wrongful act or omission on the part of the driver of the motor vehicle involved in the accident has been left to a secondary importance and mere use or involvement of motor vehicle in causing bodily injury or death to a human being or damage to property would make the petition maintainable under Sections 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicle Act. In Basant Kaur and others v. Chattar Pal Singh and others 2003 ACJ 369 MP (DB) it was observed that registration of criminal case against the driver of the offending vehicle was enough to record a finding that the driver of the offending vehicle Suit No. D464/14 was responsible for causing the accident. The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Koosappa Poojari v. K. Sadabba & Ors. MFA No.6208 of 2002 decided on 21.11.2003 observed that the driver of the vehicle Bimla Devi vs Jujjar Singh on 4 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47206546/ 6 ought to have been more prudent and circumspect while driving. It was however also observed: "But it cannot be lost sight of the fact that a duty is also cast on a pedestrian and he should use due care and caution in going upon Suit No. D464/14 and crossing the road and it is his duty to look out for on coming traffic. It is not always necessary that the vehicular traffic will have to stop for a pedestrian to cross, for the vehicle needs more time to stop in view of the speed a motor generates. In view of this, it cannot be said that it was only the driver of the vehicle in question was solely responsible for the accident." Reliance was placed in this judgment on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pramodkumar Rasikbhai Jhaveri v. Karmasey Kunvargi Tak and others (2002) 6 SCC 455 where it was observed: "The following observation of the High Court of Australia in Astley v. Austrust Ltd. ((1999) 73 ALJR 403) is worthy of quoting. A finding of contributory negligence turns on a factual investigation whether the plaintiff contributed to his or her own loss by failing to take reasonable care of his or her person or property. What is reasonable care depends on the circumstances of the case. In many cases, it may be proper for a plaintiff to rely on the defendant to perform its duty. But there is no absolute rule. The duties and responsibilities of the defendant are a variable factor in determining whether contributory negligence exists and, if so, to what degree. In some cases, the nature of the duty owed may exculpate the plaintiff from a claim of contributory Suit No. D464/14 negligence; in other cases, the nature of the duty may reduce the plaintiff's share of responsibility for the damage suffered; and in yet other cases the nature of the duty may not prevent a finding that the plaintiff failed to take reasonable care for the safety of his or her person or property. The duty owed by the defendant, although relevant, is one only of many factors that must be weighed in determining whether the plaintiff has so conducted itself that it failed to take reasonable care for the safety of its person or property." In this case the contributory negligence of the claimant was held to be 25%. Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Leela Bai v. The Managing Director & Ors. decided on 13.6.2012 held the contributory negligence of the deceased who was attempting to cross the road on the flyover to be 40%. Thus in view of the above discussion the petitioner had also contributed to the happening of the accident and as such her contributory negligence is apportioned as 25% and the negligence of Bimla Devi vs Jujjar Singh on 4 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47206546/ It was stated that due to the accident the injured fell down on the road and sustained multiple grievous injuries on various parts of her body. In T.O. Anthony v. Karvarnan & Ors., (2008) 3 SCC 748, it was held as under: "6. 'Composite negligence' refers to the negligence on the part of two or more persons. Where a person is injured as a result of negligence on the part of two or more wrongdoers, it is said that the person was injured on account of the composite negligence of those wrongdoers. In such a case, each wrongdoer is jointly and severally liable to the injured for payment of the entire damages and the injured person has the choice of proceeding against all or any of them. In such a case, the injured need not establish the extent of responsibility of each wrongdoer separately, nor is it necessary for the court to determine the extent of liability of each wrongdoer separately. Where the injured is guilty of some negligence, his claim for damages is not defeated merely by reason of the negligence on his part but the damages recoverable by him in respect of the injuries stands reduced in proportion to his contributory negligence." It has been held in Divisional Controller, K. S. R. T. C v Mahadeva Shetty and another AIR 2003 Supreme Court 4172 as under: 13."The damages for vehicular accidents are in the nature of compensation in money for loss of any kind caused to any person. In Parry V. Cleaver (1969 1 All. E. R. 555) Lord Morris stated as follows: "To compensate in money for pain and for the physical consequences is invariably difficult, but...... no other process can be devised than that of making monetary assessment." It was submitted that the petitioner got fracture in the first and second finger/right MT and great toe of her right foot and the right foot of the petitioner was injured badly and about 20 stitches were put by the doctors on her foot. It was averred that at the time of the accident, the petitioner was 61 years old and was performing her household work/ obligations very well but due to the injuries sustained by her, she was not able to do her daily routine work. It was submitted that due to the injuries, the injured as well as her family members had to suffer great mental pain, agony and financial hardship. Due to the accident, the injured had become permanently disabled as her fingers of the right foot were not working/ moving. The MLC of the petitioner is on record which shows the injuries sustained by the petitioner and as per the same the nature of injuries was opined to be grievous. The documents placed on record also show that the petitioner had sustained fracture of 1st and 2nd right metatarsal. The documents also show that she was admitted in hospital from 25.6.2014 to 26.6.2014. Thus the injuries were grievous in nature. 25. The petitioner in para 5 of her affidavit Ex.PW1/1 had stated that on the advise of doctors for her early recovery, she had to take special diet for which she had to spend a sum of Rs.300/ per day upon her special diet. During Suit No. D464/14 crossexamination by the learned counsel for the Bimla Devi vs Jujjar Singh on 4 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47206546/ 10 insurance company PW1 stated that the doctor had told her to take good diet in order to recover quickly. She denied the suggestion that she did not incur Rs.300 per day on special diet. She had not placed on record any document to show expenditure on special diet. Although the petitioner has not proved that she was advised special diet but looking at the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner notice can be taken of the fact that the petitioner might have taken diet rich in protein, vitamins and minerals for speedier recovery. In the circumstances the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/ (Rs.Five Thousand only) for special diet. 26. The petitioner in para 4 of her affidavit Ex.PW1/1 had stated that she had to hire an attendant for herself and was giving Rs.5,000/ per month for a period of 5 months. During cross examination by the learned counsel for the insurance company PW1 stated that one attendant used to look after her after the accident. She denied the suggestion that she had not engaged any attendant or that she did not incur any expenses on the same. Although the petitioner has not produced any evidence to show that she incurred any expenses towards attendant charges, however looking to the nature of injuries the petitioner would have incurred some expenditure on attendant charges and a sum of Rs.12,000/ is awarded towards attendant charges. Suit No. D464/14 LOSS OF INCOME 27. It is the case of the petitioner that at the time of the accident, the petitioner was 61 years old and was performing her household work/ obligations very well but due to the injuries sustained by her, she was not able to do her daily routine work. The petitioner had also deposed to that effect. The petitioner was not cross examined in this regard. During examination by the Tribunal the petitioner stated that she was about 60 years old. She stated that she was a housewife. 28. The petitioner has also not produced any document to show that she remained on bed rest for any particular period and there is nothing to show that she was advised bed rest for any particular period or that on account of the injuries sustained in the accident she was unable to work or to show the period for which she was not able to work. In the absence of any medical advice, notice can be taken of the fact that on account of the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner might not have been able to perform her avocation for some period. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case the petitioner is held entitled to an amount of Rs.25,000/ consolidated on account of loss of income. Suit No. D464/14 29. There is also nothing to show that the petitioner had suffered any disability on account of the injuries. The petitioner has not proved that she acquired any disability on account of the accident or that she is likely to suffer future loss of income on account of the injuries sustained in the accident and that the injuries would reduce her efficiency to work and thereby she would suffer loss of future income. Accordingly the petitioner cannot be held entitled to any amount on account of loss of future prospects. In New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sanjay Kumar & Ors. ILR 2007 (II) Delhi 733 the Hon'ble High Court observed as under: "23. The issue was considered at length by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Sanjay v. Suresh Chand & Ors. F.A.O. No.445/2000 decided on 3.8.2012 and it was observed: "The issue of satisfying the third party liability even in case of breach of the terms of insurance policy is settled by three Judge Bench report in Sohan Lal Passi v. P. Sesh Reddy, (1996) 5 SCC 21. As per Section 149(2) of the Motor Vehicles Act (the Act), an insurer is entitled to defend the action on the grounds as mentioned under Section 149(2)(a)(i)(ii) of the Act. Thus, the onus is on the insurer to prove that there is breach of the condition of the policy. Even if a conscious breach on the part of the insured is established, still the insurer has a statutory liability to pay the compensation to the third party and will simply have the right to recover the same from the insured/tortfeasor either in the same proceedings or by independent proceedings as the case may be, as ordered by the Claims Tribunal or the Court. The question of statutory liability to pay the compensation was discussed in detail by a two Judge Bench of the Supreme Court in Skandia Insurance Company Limited v. Kokilaben Chandravadan, (1987) 2 SCC 654 where it was held that exclusion clause in the contract of Insurance must be read down being in conflict with the main statutory provision enacted for protection of victim of accidents. It was laid down that the victim would be entitled to recover the compensation from the insurer irrespective of the breach of the condition of policy. The three Judge Bench of the Supreme Court in Sohan Lal Passi analyzed the corresponding provisions under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 and the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and approved the decision in Skandia. In New India Assurance Co., Shimla v. Kamla and Ors., (2001) 4 SCC 342, the Supreme Court referred to the decision of the two Judge Bench in Skandia, the three Judge Bench decision in Sohan Lal Passi and held that the insurer who has been made liable to pay the compensation to third parties on account of issuance of certificate of insurance, shall be entitled to recover the same if there was any breach of the policy condition on account of the vehicle being driven without a valid driving licence. 20. This Court in MAC APP. No.329/2010 Oriental Insurance Company Limited v. Rakesh Kumar and Others and other Appeals decided by a common judgment dated 29.02.2012, noticed some divergence of opinion in National Insurance Company Limited v. Kusum Rai & Ors., (2006) 4 SCC 250, National Insurance Company Limited v. Vidhyadhar Suit No. D464/14 Mahariwala & Ors., (2008) 12 SCC 701; Ishwar Chandra & Ors. v. The Oriental Insurance Company Limited & Ors., (2007) 10 SCC 650 and Premkumari & Ors. v. Prahalad Dev & Ors., (2008) 3 SCC 193 and held that in view of the three Judge Bench decision in Sohan Lal Passi (supra) and Swaran Singh, the liability of the Insurance Company visvis the third party is statutory. If the Insurance Company successfully proves the conscious breach of the terms of the policy, then it would be entitled to recovery rights against the owner or driver, as the case may be." Bimla Devi vs Jujjar Singh on 4 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47206546/ 14 Thus if the insurance company proves conscious breach of the terms of the policy, it would be entitled to recovery rights.

The petitioner had also deposed to that effect. The petitioner was not cross examined in this regard. During examination by the Tribunal the petitioner stated that she was about 60 years old. She stated that she was a housewife. 28. The petitioner has also not produced any document to show that she remained on bed rest for any particular period and there is nothing to show that she was advised bed rest for any particular period or that on account of the injuries sustained in the accident she was unable to work or to show the period for which she was not able to work. In the absence of any medical advice, notice can be taken of the fact that on account of the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner might not have been able to perform her avocation for some period. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case the petitioner is held entitled to an amount of Rs.25,000/ consolidated on account of loss of income. Suit No. D464/14 29. There is also nothing to show that the petitioner had suffered any disability on account of the injuries. The petitioner has not proved that she acquired any disability on account of the accident or that she is likely to suffer future loss of income on account of the injuries sustained in the accident and that the injuries would reduce her efficiency to work and thereby she would suffer loss of future income. Accordingly the petitioner cannot be held entitled to any amount on account of loss of future prospects.

It was however also observed: "But it cannot be lost sight of the fact that a duty is also cast on a pedestrian and he should use due care and caution in going upon Suit No. D464/14 and crossing the road and it is his duty to look out for on coming traffic. It is not always necessary that the vehicular traffic will have to stop for a pedestrian to cross, for the vehicle needs more time to stop in view of the speed a motor generates. In view of this, it cannot be said that it was only the driver of the vehicle in question was solely responsible for the accident." Reliance was placed in this judgment on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pramodkumar Rasikbhai Jhaveri v. Karmasey Kunvargi Tak and others (2002) 6 SCC 455 where it was observed: "The following observation of the High Court of Australia in Astley v. Austrust Ltd. ((1999) 73 ALJR 403) is worthy of quoting. A finding of contributory negligence turns on a factual investigation whether the plaintiff contributed to his or her own loss by failing to take reasonable care of his or her person or property. What is reasonable care depends on the circumstances of the case. In many cases, it may be proper for a plaintiff to rely on the defendant to perform its duty. But there is no absolute rule. The duties and responsibilities of the defendant are a variable factor in determining whether contributory negligence exists and, if so, to what degree. In some cases, the nature of the duty owed may exculpate the plaintiff from a claim of contributory Suit No. D464/14 negligence; in other cases, the nature of the duty may reduce the plaintiff's share of responsibility for the damage suffered; and in yet other cases the nature of the duty may not prevent a finding that the plaintiff failed to take reasonable care for the safety of his or her person or property. The duty owed by the defendant, although relevant, is one only of many factors that must be weighed in determining whether the plaintiff has so conducted itself that it failed to take reasonable care for the safety of its person or property." In this case the contributory negligence of the claimant was held to be 25%. Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Leela Bai v. The Managing Director & Ors. decided on 13.6.2012 held the contributory negligence of the deceased who was attempting to cross the road on the flyover to be 40%. In T.O. Anthony v. Karvarnan & Ors., (2008) 3 SCC 748, it was held as under: "6. 'Composite negligence' refers to the negligence on the part of two or more persons. Where a person is injured as a result of negligence on the part of two or more wrongdoers, it is said that the person was injured on account of the composite negligence of those wrongdoers. In such a case, each wrongdoer is jointly and severally liable to the injured for payment of the entire damages and the injured person has the choice of proceeding against all or any of them. In such a case, the injured need not establish the extent of responsibility of each wrongdoer separately, nor is it necessary for the court to determine the extent of liability of each wrongdoer separately. Where the injured is guilty of some negligence, his claim for damages is not defeated merely by reason of the negligence on his part but the damages recoverable by him in respect of the injuries stands reduced in proportion to his contributory negligence." No.445/2000 decided on 3.8.2012 and it was observed: "The issue of satisfying the third party liability even in case of breach of the terms of insurance policy is settled by three Judge Bench report in Sohan Lal Passi v. P. Sesh Reddy, (1996) 5 SCC 21. As per Section 149(2) of the Motor Vehicles Act (the Act), an insurer is entitled to defend the action on the grounds as mentioned under Section 149(2)(a)(i)(ii) of the Act. Thus, the onus is on the insurer to prove that there is breach of the condition of the policy. Even if a conscious breach on the part of the insured is established, still the insurer has a statutory liability to pay the compensation to the third party and will simply have the right to recover the same from the insured/tortfeasor either in the same proceedings or by independent proceedings as the case may be, as ordered by the Claims Tribunal or the Court. The question of statutory liability to pay the compensation was discussed in detail by a two Judge Bench of the Supreme Court in Skandia Insurance Company Limited v. Kokilaben Chandravadan, (1987) 2 SCC 654 where it was held that exclusion clause in the contract of Insurance must be read down being in conflict with the main statutory provision enacted for protection of victim of accidents. It was laid down that the victim would be entitled to recover the compensation from the insurer irrespective of the breach of the condition of policy. The three Judge Bench of the Supreme Court in Sohan Lal Passi analyzed the corresponding provisions under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 and the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and approved the decision in Skandia. In New India Assurance Co., Shimla v. Kamla and Ors., (2001) 4 SCC 342, the Supreme Court referred to the decision of the two Judge Bench in Skandia, the three Judge Bench decision in Sohan Lal Passi and held that the insurer who has been made liable to pay the compensation to third parties on account of issuance of certificate of insurance, shall be entitled to recover the same if there was any breach of the policy condition on account of the vehicle being driven without a valid driving licence. 20. This Court in MAC APP. No.329/2010 Oriental Insurance Company Limited v. Rakesh Kumar and Others and other Appeals decided by a common judgment dated 29.02.2012, noticed some divergence of opinion in National Insurance Company Limited v. Kusum Rai & Ors., (2006) 4 SCC 250, National Insurance Company Limited v. Vidhyadhar Suit No. D464/14 Mahariwala & Ors., (2008) 12 SCC 701; Ishwar Chandra & Ors. v. The Oriental Insurance Company Limited & Ors., (2007) 10 SCC 650 and Premkumari & Ors. v. Prahalad Dev & Ors., (2008) 3 SCC 193 and held that in view of the three Judge Bench decision in Sohan Lal Passi (supra) and Swaran Singh, the liability of the Insurance Company visvis the third party is statutory. If the Insurance Company successfully proves the conscious breach of the terms of the policy, then it would be entitled to recovery rights against the owner or driver, as the case may be."
